To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the expression of biotransfomation genes was increased by raw OSPW, and decreased by ozone treatment, (2) the expression of cardiac development genes was not associated with any changes in cardiac function and (3) the expression of apoptotic genes was not associated to any morphological changes.
the expression of Cyp1 genes was increased after raw OSPW exposure and that the development of the heart was not associated with changes in heart rate or heart size.

raw and ozonized OSPW did not affect the development and survival of zebafish, however, raw OSPW exposure induced the expression of biotransforming genes CYP1B and CYP1A while ozonized OSPWs only slightly induced Cyp1b.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the potential effects of OSPW and ozone-treated OSPW on zebrafish development and gene expression, and how these changes are associated with whole organism endpoints.
the potential for OSPW to be released into the environment.
the development of a more holistic assessment of the effects of OSPWs and their remediation on developing organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ozone treatment of OSPW reduced the toxicity associated with the raw OSPW, however, the effects of ozonated OSPWs on developing zebafish embryos was not completely eliminated.

ozone treatment reduced the amount of NAs present in OSPW and decreased the expression of Cyp1a and Cyp1b genes in zebrafish, but it did not affect the development of the heart or other organ systems.
the ozone-treated OSPW was not as toxic as raw OSPW.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ozone treatment decreased the toxicity of OSPW, as it reduced the concentration of NAs, but it did not reduce the toxicity of the remaining NAs in the sample.
ozone treatment reduced the toxicity of the OSPW by reducing its concentration of naphthenate acids.
ozone treatment of OSPW reduced toxicity and biomarker expression, but did not eliminate it completely.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gene expression is not always indicative of whole organism level effects.
ozone treatment reduced the amount of NAs in OSPW by 92% and that this decrease was reflected in the lower levels of gene induction observed in zebrafish.
the use of ozone treatment can decrease the toxicity of OSPW and that gene expression can be used as a biomarker of exposure, but may not be indicative of adverse outcomes.
